findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The guidance asks for a load reproduction and a soak run but omits how to do them, and the producer's command policy denies shell loops.
findings.evidence: policy.rs:6-10 splits Bash at &&, ;, | and newlines, and requires each segment's program to be on the role's list. It denies subshells, substitution and brace expansion. athena.toml:84 gives the change producer only cargo, git, ls, rm, mv and chmod, so `for`/`seq`/`bash` loops are refused. The 9daz introspection reported that no recorded 200-run loop was run. Without a stated way to do this, the new text repeats the gap it is meant to close. crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs shows the way that works: a test that loops CYCLES=200 times with WRITERS and FORKERS threads inside a single `cargo test`. Fix: Say how in the paragraph. For example: reproduce and soak with a test that loops the racy action many times on parallel threads and counts failures (as crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs does), run with `cargo test`, because shell loops are denied. Add a pinned phrase for this (for example 'loops' or 'stand_in_stress') to the unit test, and name it in the criterion 1 demonstration.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (suggested paragraph text) and step 2 (pinned phrases); crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs:6-10; athena.toml:84

findings.summary: A 470-byte cap does not guarantee the set stays within 1200 tokens.
findings.evidence: The budget line is 1043 of 1200, so 157 tokens are left. A 469-byte paragraph plus the two-byte blank-line separator is 471 bytes, ⌈471/3⌉ = 157 tokens, so the set lands exactly on 1200 with nothing to spare. The suggested text is about 380 bytes (my estimate), so it fits, but the stated cap does not protect anything. Fix: Cap the paragraph at about 420 bytes and keep reading the exact size from the budget test's failure message, as step 3 already does.
findings.location: Files: producer.md entry; Risks, first bullet

findings.summary: The wording requires a shared helper and a scan test for every intermittent failure, including one-off races where no repeated pattern exists.
findings.evidence: The 9daz flake in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs was a single-site race, not a pattern repeated across call sites. As written, the rule pushes producers to invent a helper and a scan where neither fits, which a senior reviewer would reject as over-general. Fix: Make that part conditional: 'when the same pattern is at more than one site, fix it once in a shared helper and add a repo test that finds every site'. Keep 'fix it where it starts' unconditional.
findings.location: Step 1 suggested text: 'Fix it where it starts, in one shared helper and not at each call site, and add a repo test that scans for every site'

findings.summary: The planner also lacked this design information, and the plan does not name it as a follow-up.
findings.evidence: The failure class is named '...-supplies-design', and the recorded cause is 'no root-cause design'. Design comes from the planner, whose always-loaded set is 1105 of 1200 (system facts). The producer follows the accepted plan, so a plan that patches call sites would still steer the producer. The root-cause default says: 'when that lies outside the job's scope, name it and propose the fix'. Fix: In D189 and the change description, name the planner brief as a stage that also lacked this guidance, and propose a follow-up (for example one sentence in the planner frame, which has about 95 tokens left).

findings.summary: Appending the paragraph after the closing 'Before you report…' line means the producer's last instruction is no longer the report step.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/producer.md:3 ends with 'Before you report, reread the brief's criteria_check section…', a step meant to come last. Fix: Insert the new paragraph before the final report sentence (split it into its own paragraph if needed), and adjust the blank-line assertion to match.
findings.location: Step 1: 'Append to producer.md a blank line and one prose paragraph'

summary: The plan follows the accepted reading. It adds flaky-test guidance to the change producer section, which is compiled in by include_str! at crates/athena-cap-change/src/lib.rs:21 and returned by producer_section() at :51. A new unit test in the existing tests module (:118) pins the guidance. The plan also records the one-number budget-line edit that the budget test forces, as commit d94ebc2 did. I read the files and checked these claims, and they hold: computed_rows takes the largest producer set (budgets.rs:42-61), check_system_facts reports the drift (:109-114), the context tests compare the file on disk with the compiled text (context lib.rs:445, :820), and the Unreleased / Changed section of CHANGELOG.md exists. The demonstrations use real seams and would fail without the change. One major gap remains. The producer's Bash policy splits commands into segments and allows only listed programs: athena.toml:84 lists cargo/git/ls/rm/mv/chmod, and crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs:6-10 denies subshells, substitution and brace expansion. So a shell loop such as `for i in ...; do cargo test; done` is denied. The new paragraph tells the producer to reproduce under load and report a soak run, but not how to do that under the policy. That is the same information gap behind job 9daz's missing 200-run loop. The tree already holds the pattern that works: crates/athena-testkit/tests/stand_in_stress.rs runs WRITERS×CYCLES iterations with threads inside one cargo test. The rest are minor: the byte cap sits on the budget edge, the wording is too broad for one-off races, and the planner gap goes unnamed.
